type:
∀ {R : Type u} [Ring R] {I : Type v} (M : I → ModuleCat.{max v w} R),
  letI : DecidableEq I := Classical.decEq I
  let inclusion := DirectSum.coeFnLinearMap R (ι := I) (M := fun i => ↥(M i))
  Nonempty (CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit
    (CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.mk (ModuleCat.of R (∀ i : I, ↥(M i)))
      (fun i => ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.proj i)))) ∧
  Nonempty (CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit
    (CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.mk (ModuleCat.of R (DirectSum I (fun i => ↥(M i))))
      (fun i => ModuleCat.ofHom (DirectSum.lof R I (fun j => ↥(M j)) i)))) ∧
  Function.Injective inclusion ∧
  (∀ x : ∀ i : I, ↥(M i), x ∈ Set.range inclusion ↔ Set.Finite {i : I | x i ≠ 0})
sourceReason:
The cached TeX and PDF agree on Proposition 5.7 (env-5-7, p. 16) of Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules. The statement gives the universal properties for the tuple module with coordinate projections and the direct sum with coordinate inclusions. The direct sum is embedded linearly in the tuple module and its range is exactly the finite-support tuples. The indexing type may be infinite or empty. The bundled module universe is chosen large enough for the indexing type. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=16

The configured defect report returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction for Proposition 5.7 was available there. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects

The owner confirms the notes’ ordinary-choice convention for unital modules over arbitrary unital rings. Classical.decEq supplies index equality internally. The shared-slot check used ModuleCat.productConeIsLimit and ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit from the pinned Mathlib revision. Lean reported propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as the theorem’s axioms.
